items.title: Denise Morel Interview, 1965-05-07
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...Have you heard Bonnie Bigard...? [INTERVIEWEE] The first time I heard Armstrong with Barnaby Bigard...

ctx.x: Oh, he is very few known. In fact, the French people know the big names, that's to say Armstrong, obviously, Bichet, because he is here in France. But they know King Oliver very few, and Johnny Dodds, I don't think, but there are only some fans, some specialists who they know. And we have a lot of trouble finding Johnny Dodds in France. We know General Morton. General Morton was more known than Johnny Dodds. Maybe because the piano is a more commercial instrument than the clarinet, or more easy.
Well, what do you think about the New Orleans musicians who have come there in person? Have you heard Bonnie Bigard, Albert Nicholas, any of those? Yes.

The first time I heard Armstrong with Barnaby Bigard, I was a bit upset because I found that he was making a commercial music. It had a bit of a fabric, a lack of spontaneity. And when I saw Joe Killington when he was in Paris, it was even worse. I thought it was terrible. It was all except jazz. And they were very surprised by the exigence of the French public They thought that the French were more exigent. They thought that the French were more exigent than the American.
